search_text.description: Searches for a text substring within project files. Returns one entry per file with match coordinates (1-based line and column, end exclusive).

params.paths: Glob patterns relative to the project root, with optional '!' excludes. A pattern without '/' matches the file name anywhere. A trailing '/' expands to '**'.
params.limit: Maximum number of results to return

search_regex.description: Searches for regular expression matches within project files. Returns one entry per file with match coordinates (1-based line and column, end exclusive).

params.paths: Glob patterns relative to the project root, with optional '!' excludes. A pattern without '/' matches the file name anywhere. A trailing '/' expands to '**'.
params.limit: Maximum number of results to return

search_symbol.description: Searches for symbols: classes, methods, and fields. Use it for semantic lookup by identifier fragments. By default it searches project symbols only; repeat with include_external=true to search SDK and library symbols too.

params.paths: Glob patterns relative to the project root, with optional '!' excludes. A pattern without '/' matches the file name anywhere. A trailing '/' expands to '**'.
params.include_external: Whether to include SDK and library symbols. Try it when the project search found nothing suitable.
params.limit: Maximum number of results to return

rename_refactoring.description: Renames a symbol (variable, method, class, etc.) in the specified file and updates all references throughout the project. Use this instead of search-and-replace for safe, context-aware renaming.

params.pathInProject: Relative path to the file from the project root directory
params.symbolName: Exact, case-sensitive name of the existing symbol to rename
params.newName: New, case-sensitive name for the symbol

move_method.description: Moves a Java method from its containing class to a target class, updating all call sites. Static methods are moved as static members; instance methods are moved onto a target-typed parameter or field.

params.pathInProject: Relative path to the Java file from the project root
params.methodName: Exact name of the method to move
params.targetClass: Fully-qualified name of the destination class, e.g. "org.acme.Bar"
params.parameterTypes: Optional parameter types to disambiguate overloaded methods, e.g. ["String", "int"]

extract_method.description: Extracts the code fragment at the given line/column range of a Java file into a new method, replacing the selection with a call site. The range uses 1-based inclusive line/column coordinates.

params.pathInProject: Relative path to the Java file from the project root
params.startLine: 1-based line number of the first selected line
params.startColumn: 1-based column number of the first selected character (default: 1)
params.endLine: 1-based line number of the last selected line
params.endColumn: 1-based column number of the last selected character, inclusive (default: end of line)
params.methodName: Name for the extracted method; a safe name is suggested automatically if omitted

introduce_parameter.description: Replaces a local variable with a new method parameter, updating all call sites of the method in the project. The local declaration is removed and every occurrence becomes a reference to the new parameter.

params.pathInProject: Relative path to the Java file from the project root
params.variableName: Exact name of the local variable to replace with the new parameter
params.methodName: Optional name of the method declaring the variable, to disambiguate when several methods declare a variable with the same name
params.parameterTypes: Optional method parameter types to disambiguate overloaded methods, e.g. ["String", "int"]

pull_up_method.description: Pulls a Java method up from its containing class into a superclass, updating all references with it. When makeAbstract is set the superclass keeps an abstract declaration and the implementation stays in the source class.

params.pathInProject: Relative path to the Java file from the project root
params.methodName: Exact name of the method to pull up
params.parameterTypes: Optional parameter types to disambiguate overloaded methods, e.g. ["String", "int"]
params.targetClass: Fully-qualified name of the destination superclass; defaults to the direct superclass
params.makeAbstract: When true, the superclass receives an abstract declaration and the implementation stays in the source class

push_down_method.description: Pushes a Java method down from a superclass into one or all of its direct subclasses, updating references. Without a targetClass the method is pushed into all direct subclasses and kept abstract in the source class.

params.pathInProject: Relative path to the Java file from the project root
params.methodName: Exact name of the method to push down
params.parameterTypes: Optional parameter types to disambiguate overloaded methods, e.g. ["String", "int"]
params.targetClass: Fully-qualified name of a single destination subclass; when omitted, all direct subclasses receive the method

inline_method.description: Inlines a Java method into all of its call sites, replacing each call with the method body. Optionally removes the now-empty method declaration.

params.pathInProject: Relative path to the Java file from the project root
params.methodName: Exact name of the method to inline
params.parameterTypes: Optional parameter types to disambiguate overloaded methods, e.g. ["String", "int"]
params.inlineThisOnly: Inline only the single existing call site instead of all usages (default: false)
params.deleteMethod: Remove the method declaration after inlining all usages (default: true)

safe_delete.description: Safely deletes a class, method, field, parameter or local variable after verifying that every usage in the project can be resolved by the IntelliJ Safe Delete refactoring.

params.pathInProject: Relative path to the Java file from the project root
params.symbolName: Exact name of the symbol to delete
params.kind: Optional element kind to disambiguate: "class", "method", "field", "parameter" or "local" (default: auto)
